figmaExecutionNotes: Follow the provided content map exactly; do not reword hero or section copy.
Use a strong trust-first hierarchy in the first viewport with logo/badge emphasis.
No pricing, testimonials, forms, or news sections are supported by the input, so do not add them.
Maintain consistent 24px card padding, 12px radius, and design-system spacing.
Mobile should collapse grids to single-column stacks, keep CTAs stacked full-width, and preserve content order from desktop.
If product imagery is unavailable, use non-decorative placeholders only as structural anchors; do not leave large empty spaces.

heroStrategy.headline: Elevate Your Team’s Productivity with Zoho Workplace
heroStrategy.subheadline: A complete email and collaboration suite for enterprises that unifies communication, documents, meetings, and team workflows in one secure workspace.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use an unexpected editorial-over-dashboards composition: a full-bleed mesh-gradient hero with layered enterprise UI cards floating on the right and a compact trust band under the copy. Keep the red brand accent for CTAs and key highlights, use a dark feature section later in the page for contrast, and alternate subsequent feature blocks left/right with light/dark treatment. Headline must be oversized and dominant, with the product UI acting as proof rather than decoration.

repetitionBreakers: Hero is split and media-led; trust immediately follows as a static logo grid; product section uses spotlight-plus-grid instead of another card grid; testimonials use a 3-card grid; pricing becomes a centered highlighted card; lead form is a floating card to re-accelerate conversion.
No adjacent sections share the same background tone; white and soft-slate alternate throughout.
Feature density changes by section: concise in hero, structured in products, compact in pricing, more emotional in testimonials.
blueprint.pageTitle: Zoho Workplace for Enterprises | Unified Email and Collaboration Suite
blueprint.metaDescription: Explore Zoho Workplace, an enterprise email and collaboration suite for unified communication, real-time teamwork, secure access, and faster productivity across your organization.

sections.backgroundTreatment: soft white-to-slate enterprise field with layered product panels and subtle red emphasis accents
sections.designNote: Content-first split hero that answers what this is, who it is for, and what to do next. Use the headline to match the ad message and keep the subheadline enterprise-specific. Right side should show stacked UI panels for mail, chat, docs, meetings, and storage to make the suite feel tangible. CTA is a solid full-opacity accent button labeled exactly Get started.

Place trust early because the traffic is warm and proof type is logos. Show 3-6 recognisable customer logos in a clean static grid; if actual logos are unavailable, fall back to a metric strip. Keep this section visually restrained so it supports rather than competes with the hero.

Use a spotlight panel for the core click-driving promise: unified email, chat, docs, meetings, and storage in one workspace. Follow with a structured grid for the remaining 1-2 strongest differentiators only, not a generic SaaS feature dump. Keep the first product block visually expressive with a preview panel; the next block can switch to a tighter support grid for integrations and mobility. Since there are multiple productSections, alternate the internal layouts between spotlight-plus-grid and split-panel-list rather than repeating a flat card grid.

This section is intentionally omitted from content emphasis because include=false. If rendered for template consistency, keep it minimal and utility-focused, such as a short grid of buying-support points. Do not elevate it above proof or features.

Make pricing a clean centered card with a premium enterprise feel. Include the plan name and the included value stack, but avoid cluttering the card with comparisons. Use the CTA Get started as the only button label. This section should feel conversion-led without becoming aggressive.

With 4+ testimonials available, use a 3-card grid or a restrained carousel-static pattern. Prioritize the most specific operational outcomes: streamlined communication, easier collaboration, and reduced tool dependency. Keep the cards emotionally credible, not overly promotional.

A floating lead form card should close the page with a low-friction conversion moment. Keep it visually distinct from prior sections and more compact than the pricing card. Because CTA aggression is moderate, do not add extra secondary actions; use the single required CTA label Get started and make it full-width on mobile.

Do not use a moving marquee unless explicitly required. Since the available content does not include strong media logos, keep this section optional or convert it into a minimal confidence strip only if needed. Otherwise, omit to preserve rhythm and avoid redundant proof.

blueprint.designPersonality: An organized, modern enterprise dashboard aesthetic: clean white canvas, red brand confidence, modular cards, logo-first trust, and highly scannable feature architecture designed to convert enterprise buyers quickly.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use enterprise software UI mockups, app tiles, and logo-heavy proof bands. The hero should show a polished workspace dashboard with email, chat, docs, meetings, and storage represented as layered panels. Integrations should be visualized as compact logo chips or app badges. Keep the page premium but practical, with strong whitespace and a conversion-first trust hierarchy.

referenceMap.heroPattern: single-column hero with brand/logo at top, large headline, short supporting paragraph, and a compact benefits list; no split-media hero or prominent illustration visible in the reference HTML
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: hero first, then lead-capture form, then stacked content sections; structure appears linear and conversion-focused rather than modular dashboard-style
referenceMap.cardStyle: form card with solid surface and simple container treatment; no evidence of glassmorphism, hover-elevated feature cards, or masonry layouts in the provided HTML
referenceMap.ctaPattern: primary conversion CTA embedded in lead form context rather than repeated sticky or segmented CTAs; pattern favors one dominant action and form submission flow
referenceMap.mediaPattern: minimal media usage; logo only in hero area, no visible product screenshots, video embeds, or media panels in the provided HTML
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: stacked feature sections with headline, short description, and grouped feature lists; likely intended for progressive disclosure through section-by-section reading rather than tabs or accordions
referenceMap.formPattern: lead-generation form card placed immediately after hero; multiple hidden tracking fields indicate conversion-oriented capture and attribution logic
referenceMap.animationStyle: static presentation with no explicit animation cues in the provided HTML
componentPatterns: benefit bullet list with icon ticks
designNotes: No interactive navigation patterns visible in supplied HTML
Use simple, high-contrast hierarchy and restrained visual complexity
Trust signaling is implied through copy and tracking structure rather than visible badges in the HTML snippet

mustHaveMoments: Prominent logo/trust strip immediately after the hero to reinforce the 100,000+ businesses proof
Concise hero with the exact product promise, one primary CTA and one secondary trial CTA
Fast scan feature stack focused on unified workspace, real-time collaboration, remote access, and AI assistance
Integrated app ecosystem section to show extensibility and workflow fit
Pricing/includes section that clearly lists what is included in the plan
Multiple testimonial blocks to support enterprise confidence and reduce risk
Clear support/migration/onboarding reassurance near conversion points
avoidPatterns: Split hero layouts that overemphasize imagery and dilute the message
Empty or oversized feature cards that create too much whitespace without visual content
Strip-heavy layouts that feel repetitive and reduce perceived value
Missing pricing/cart section or unclear purchase path
Generic stock visuals that do not add product credibility
Overly editorial storytelling that slows the conversion flow
Mismatched hero copy that drifts from the provided content
designStrategy.reasoning: Zoho Workplace is a familiar B2B productivity suite, so the page should convert warm enterprise traffic with proof and clarity rather than discovery. The strongest trust signal in the brief is logo/social proof, so the design should foreground the 100,000+ businesses message early and repeatedly. A centered, message-first hero keeps the value proposition sharp and supports a fast scan path into features, integrations, testimonials, and pricing. Because the page goal is lead generation, the CTA pattern should be assertive but not aggressive, with easy entry to a free trial and a clear get-started path. The overall layout should stay balanced and conversion-centric, with enough visual rhythm to avoid the repetitive strip problem while keeping content dense enough for enterprise evaluation.
